collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A child tells others a villager's flaking skin is catching: say something yourself, or ask a healer to talk to the children.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has a skin condition that comes and goes: rough, flaking patches on (subject.his/her) arms and elbows. It doesn't hurt much and it isn't catching. But today (subject.he/she) has heard (friend) whispering to other children by the stream: "Don't touch (subject.him/her). You'll get it too." Some of the children have stepped back.

choices.label: Ask (healer) to Talk to the Children

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) walks over and sits down by the stream, calm. "You can't catch it," (subject.he/she) says. "It's just how my skin is. It's been like this since I was your age. Ask the healers if you don't believe me." (friend) goes red. Some of the children do ask the healers. The healers say the same. (friend) doesn't apologize that day. A week later (friend.he/she) hands (subject) a mango without a word.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) is tired, and asks (healer), a healer, to speak to the children instead. (healer) sits them down and explains, plainly, that some skin is just different, that it isn't catching, and that whispering things that aren't true about people makes them feel very alone. (friend) is quiet for a long time. The next day (friend.he/she) sits next to (subject) at the fire and asks, nervously, if it itches. (subject) says sometimes. That's the start.
